# Offline fixtures

`readable.pdf` and `image-only.pdf` are deterministic project-generated PDF 1.4 fixtures. Regenerate them from the repository root with `node packages/searxng-suite/test/fixtures/generate-pdfs.mjs` (Node standard library only). The readable fixture contains `OFFLINE_PDF_FIXTURE` using the standard Helvetica font without an embedded font program. The image-only fixture contains one project-defined RGB pixel scaled into a rectangle, with no text or fonts. Neither file contains author/build/timestamp metadata or third-party document/image/font data. Tests use the existing unpdf dependency and need no PDF converter at runtime. Invalid-PDF input is generated in the tests.

`pdf.mjs` is a test-only replacement for unpdf inside real Node worker threads. It reads a small JSON scenario, verifies the original was published before parser entry, and emits trace events for page scheduling/cleanup. Its CPU-busy and asynchronous stalls write heartbeats to prove they started. Tests snapshot actual worker-exit events immediately when tool execution resolves, before artifact IO, and separately hold the termination promise to verify it is awaited. There are no post-exit sleeps. It is not a PDF parser or a benchmark.

`undici.mjs` retains the installed Node Undici implementation and Agent. It substitutes fetch responses only when a test explicitly supplies one. The connector checks leave fetch untouched and feed actual Undici HTTP parsing through controlled in-memory duplex sockets and mocked DNS. Other TCP/TLS connections and listening sockets are blocked, including in child Node processes. Callback/promise DNS lookup, resolve and reverse entrypoints, including Resolver instances, are blocked unless the test explicitly controls the callback lookup. This is an API-level test guard, not an OS network sandbox.

All fixtures, hooks, helpers and tests stay outside the npm payload. Temporary PDFs, text/JSON outputs, traces, configurations and tarballs are created under the runner's private temporary root and removed when the run finishes, including test failures. No session history or real search credentials are used as fixtures.
